html:
Philip II was king of Macedon from 359 BCE until he was murdered in 336 BCE. In about twenty years he turned a weak kingdom on the edge of the Greek world into the master of Greece, and left his son Alexander the army that conquered Persia.

As a young man he spent years as a hostage in Thebes, where he watched the army of Epaminondas. As king he built a new army: infantry with very long pikes, the sarissa, in a deep phalanx, working with heavy Companion cavalry. Gold mines in Thrace paid for it. He used bribes and marriages as freely as force.

  • He took the Greek cities on the north Aegean coast, which brought him into conflict with Athens and the speeches of Demosthenes.
  • He ended the Third Sacred War in 346 BCE and gained a voice at Delphi.
  • He beat Athens and Thebes at the Battle of Chaeronea in 338 BCE and formed the League of Corinth to lead Greece against the Persian Empire.

He hired Aristotle to teach Alexander, his son by Olympias. He was stabbed by a bodyguard at a wedding feast at Aegae as he prepared to invade Persia.
sum: Philip II was king of Macedon from 359 BCE until he was murdered in 336 BCE. In about twenty years he turned a weak kingdom on the edge of the Greek world into the master of Greece, and left his son Alexander the army that conquered Persia.
